set.body:
Raised while Epic 8 is in progress, before the gate is run and its numbers are certified.

The gate harness itself is well built - isolated worker process, 4 GiB and 30-minute thresholds, real RSS capture via .current_rss_bytes(), a genuine neuroim2 volume domain, a dense shrinkage_precision metric and an explicit exclude_evaluation training policy. No complaint about the machinery.

The FIXTURE is the problem. Measured on the exact gate geometry (full_dim 52x42x25, 24 active slices, spacing 3mm, radius 6.1mm):

  features (voxels)                        52416      <- good, hits the 50-60k target
  support size                             min 11, median 33, mean 31.2, max 33
  observations per run                     32,  design columns 2  -> residual df per run = 30
  partitions                               3,   exclude_evaluation -> 1 training run per edge
  total residual df for Sigma-hat per edge 30

  supports with k > available df (30)      83.9%
  supports with k > df/2                   99.9%

So for 84% of searchlights the local sample covariance is SINGULAR before shrinkage, and for essentially all of them it is ill-conditioned. shrinkage_precision(0.2) is not regularizing an estimate, it is supplying one. The metric is determined by the shrinkage target rather than by the data.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THIS EPIC SPECIFICALLY

Epic 8 acceptance opens with "Establish the actual supported regime instead of promising that every local dense metric scales." The timing and memory numbers this gate produces will be perfectly valid as linear-algebra cost - a k-by-k solve costs the same whether the input is well conditioned or not - but they would be recorded as evidence that brain-scale dense local metrics work, in a configuration where no searchlight has enough data to estimate one.

It also lands in the worst corner of the learner-quality effect measured in Epic 7: three partitions under exclude_evaluation leaves exactly ONE training run per edge, the minimum possible, which is the data-starved arm that produced the largest metric bias in that study.

CHEAP FIX - either alone is sufficient to make k < df

  - raise observations per run: 32 -> 200 gives 198 df per run
  - or raise partitions: 3 -> 6 gives 4 training runs per edge, 120 df

With 6 runs at 30 df each, k = 33 sits at df/k ~ 3.6, which is a defensible regime. Raising observations is closer to real task-fMRI and costs only simulation time, not gate runtime, since the residual statistics are accumulated once per partition.

Recommend also recording the realised df-to-support ratio in the gate output, so the certified artifact states the regime it measured rather than leaving it to be inferred.

Not a defect in the harness, and the performance evidence is still worth collecting. The issue is what the numbers will be taken to prove.
set.title: Crossnobis scale gate times a statistically degenerate fixture: local covariance singular for 84% of supports
